metadata.title: Quantum Dot Confinement — Color Right, Y-Axis Wrong
metadata.purpose: Critique the Brus equation quantum-dot-confinement D3 visualization — its encodings, what it gets right, what it hides, and the one fix that matters.

beats.narration_text: Salut. One prompt to Claude: build a Brus equation visualization for quantum dot confinement. Here is what came back — and here is what I think of it. I'm Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for quantum dot confinement.
output: ✓ Band gap vs radius, experimental overlay

beats.narration_text: Four panels. Main plot: band gap energy in electron-volts against dot radius in nanometers, one to ten, linear axes. Red Brus theory curve. Seven black experimental data points. Controls right: material toggle, radius slider, color swatch, Brus Terms bar chart. Below: a log-log confinement panel and a physics console.

Drag R left: smaller dot, higher confinement energy E_conf — it scales as one over R-squared. Band gap rises. The color swatch jumps from red toward orange, then blue-violet at the smallest radii. Drag right: bigger dot, E_conf drops, wavelength redshifts toward near-infrared. The log-log panel shows the same motion as a straight line, slope minus two.

The color swatch is the standout encoding. As R shrinks, the sim converts E_dot to a photon wavelength via 1240 divided by E, then maps that to an actual rendered color. Students see quantum confinement as a visible color shift — not a number. That is the encoding doing real work.

The log-log panel earns its space. Plotting confinement energy alone removes the additive bulk constant, isolating the pure R-squared power law. The slope label is on the curve. Students can measure it. That makes the law checkable, not just memorized.

The theory-versus-experiment overlay is honest. The Brus curve lies above the CdSe data points at small R. The viz does not hide that mismatch by cropping the x-axis or smoothing the data to the theory. It shows where the effective-mass model fails — and lets students ask why.

Three problems, all fixable.

First: the y-axis auto-rescales when you switch materials. Toggle from CdSe to ZnS and the energy range silently shifts. You cannot see that ZnS has a bulk gap twice as large. The toggle implies a comparison — the y-axis makes it impossible. Fix: lock the axis from one to seven electron-volts and plot both curves simultaneously.

Second: the Brus Terms bar chart is too small to be useful. At 280 by 90 pixels with nine-point labels, the Coulomb correction bar — the only negative term in the Brus equation — is a hairline at large R and clips off the bottom. That bar is the argument; it needs to be readable.

Third: the physics console rubber-stamps itself. P3 reports 0.01 percent agreement between theory and experiment at R equals five nanometers. The experimental value in the code was evidently chosen to match the theory output, not taken from an independent measurement. A check that always passes teaches students that agreement equals validity.

Let's recap with Claude. A physically honest Brus equation interactive — the color swatch makes quantum confinement visible. Use it at the start of a quantum dots lecture. Stay in CdSe mode until the y-axis is fixed. The one change that matters: lock the axis and plot both materials simultaneously so the toggle teaches the comparison it implies.

props.artifactTitle: Quantum Dot Confinement — Brus Equation Viz
artifactLines: Color swatch → emission wavelength: the win.
Log–log slope = −2: power law made checkable.
Lock the axis. Plot both materials. Ship it.

beats.narration_text: I have a D3.js Brus equation simulator for quantum dot confinement in CdSe and ZnS. A material toggle switches between the two, but the y-axis auto-rescales on each switch, making it impossible to compare the two materials visually. Fix this by: one, locking the y-axis from 1.0 to 7.0 electron-volts for both materials; two, plotting both Brus theory curves simultaneously in two distinct colors with a legend; and three, keeping both experimental datasets visible as differently-shaped markers. While you are in the code, enlarge the Brus Terms bar chart to at least 280 by 200 pixels and increase the label font size to 12 points so the Coulomb correction bar is readable at all radii.
